easy.def: A person who does something for fun, not as a job.
examples: He is an amateur painter.
The amateur played well.
She is an amateur.

more.def: A person who does something for enjoyment and not as a paid job.
examples: He is an amateur painter who paints on weekends.
The amateur played in the park.
The amateurs and professionals played on the same field.

easy.def: To surprise someone a lot.
examples: The magic trick will amaze you.
Her fast running amazed us.
The big fireworks amaze me.

more.def: To fill someone with great surprise or wonder.
examples: The size of the whale amazed everyone on the boat.
It amazes me how many stars you can see in the desert.
The young chess player amazed the crowd with her skill.

easy.def: Very surprised.
examples: I was amazed.
She was amazed by the trick.
He looked amazed.

more.def: Filled with great surprise and wonder.
examples: I was amazed by the magic trick.
She was amazed at how tall the tree was.
The kids looked amazed at the huge cake.

easy.def: Great surprise.
examples: She stared in amazement.
His eyes opened in amazement.
We watched in amazement.

more.def: A feeling of great surprise and wonder.
examples: She stared in amazement at the huge cake.
The children watched the magician in amazement.
He shook his head in amazement.

easy.def: Very surprising and wonderful.
examples: The magic show was amazing.
What an amazing view!
She did an amazing jump.

more.def: So surprising or wonderful that it is hard to believe.
examples: The acrobats did amazing flips.
The view from the mountain top was amazing.
It is amazing how fast a cheetah can run.

easy.def: In a way that is very surprising.
examples: The bird sang amazingly well.
He jumped amazingly high.
She ran amazingly fast.

more.def: In a way that is so great or surprising that you feel amazed.
examples: The little girl danced amazingly well.
He amazingly escaped without a scratch.
The cake tasted amazingly good.

easy.def: A person who represents their country in another country.
examples: The ambassador met the king.
The ambassador lives abroad.
The ambassador gave a speech.

more.def: A person chosen to represent their country in another country.
examples: The ambassador met with the leaders of the other country.
She served as ambassador for three years.
The ambassador gave a speech in French.

easy.def: A shiny golden-brown stone.
examples: The amber is shiny.
She wore an amber necklace.
Amber is golden.

more.def: A hard, clear, yellow-brown substance that is made from the sap of ancient trees.
examples: The insect was trapped in a piece of amber.
Tiny bubbles were frozen inside the amber.
Amber glows golden in the sunlight.

easy.def: A yellow-orange color.
examples: The light is amber.
The traffic light turned amber.
The leaves turned amber.

more.def: A color that is a mix of yellow and orange.
examples: The room glowed with amber light from the lamp.
The leaves turned a deep amber in autumn.
The honey was a clear amber color.

easy.def: A big goal that you want to reach.
examples: Her ambition is to be a doctor.
He has big ambition.
My ambition is to fly.

more.def: A strong wish to do or become something important.
examples: Her ambition is to be a doctor when she grows up.
He has the ambition to run in the Olympics.
Her ambition to build a robot kept her studying every night.

easy.def: Wanting to do something big and working hard for it.
examples: She is an ambitious girl.
An ambitious plan.
He is ambitious.

more.def: Having a strong wish to do or achieve something big, and being willing to work hard for it.
examples: She is an ambitious student who wants to be a scientist.
The class had an ambitious plan to build a whole model city.
He is ambitious and practices for hours every day.

easy.def: To walk in a slow, easy way.
examples: We ambled home.
The cow ambles along.
They ambled to the park.

more.def: To walk slowly and easily, with no hurry.
examples: We ambled along the beach and looked for shells.
The cows ambled across the field.
Grandpa ambled down the road with his dog.

easy.def: A truck that takes hurt people to the hospital.
examples: The ambulance came fast.
An ambulance has a siren.
The ambulance took her to the hospital.

more.def: A special vehicle that carries sick or hurt people to a hospital.
examples: The ambulance raced to the hospital with its siren on.
Cars pulled over to let the ambulance go by.
The helpers in the ambulance cared for the hurt man.

easy.def: A word said at the end of a prayer.
examples: They said amen at the end.
The class said amen together.
We all said amen.

more.def: A word used at the end of a prayer that means "may it be so."
examples: The people said amen when the prayer was over.
Everyone in the church said amen together.
He bowed his head and said amen.

easy.def: To change something to make it better.
examples: We amended the rule.
She amended her story.
Let's amend the plan.

more.def: To change or fix something, such as a rule, a law or a piece of writing, to make it better.
examples: The class voted to amend the rule so everyone gets a turn.
She amended her story to fix a few mistakes.
The town council amended the law to allow bikes on the path.

easy.def: A change or addition to a law or rule.
examples: The amendment changed the rule.
We read an amendment.
The class voted on the amendment.

more.def: A change or addition made to a law, rule or piece of writing.
examples: The class voted for an amendment to the rules of the game.
The First Amendment to the Constitution protects free speech.
The mayor added an amendment to the town's new law.

easy.def: A purple jewel.
examples: The ring has an amethyst.
An amethyst is purple.
She found an amethyst.

more.def: A clear purple stone that is used in jewelry.
examples: The necklace had a large amethyst in the middle.
The amethyst sparkled in the light.
Amethysts grow inside rocks as clusters of purple crystals.

easy.def: In the middle of.
examples: The house stood amid the trees.
Amid the noise, she heard it.
He smiled amid the crowd.

more.def: In the middle of, or surrounded by.
examples: The house stood amid tall trees.
Amid the noise, I heard my name.
He sat calmly amid the chaos.

easy.def: In the middle of.
examples: The cat sat amidst the toys.
We played amidst the trees.
Amidst the noise, he read.

more.def: In the middle of or surrounded by something.
examples: The cat slept amidst a pile of pillows.
We played amidst the tall trees.
Amidst the noise of the crowd, he found his friend.

easy.def: Wrong.
examples: Something is amiss.
Nothing was amiss.
I felt something amiss.

more.def: Not right; wrong in some way.
examples: The dog sensed that something was amiss.
Nothing seemed amiss when we got home.
She felt something was amiss when the lights were off.

easy.def: A strong liquid or gas with a sharp smell, used for cleaning.
examples: Ammonia has a strong smell.
Never smell ammonia.
Ammonia cleans windows.

more.def: A gas with a very strong, sharp smell, or the liquid cleaner made from it, which can be harmful if you breathe it in.
examples: The cleaner contains ammonia, so we opened the windows.
Ammonia has a strong smell that can sting your nose.
Never mix ammonia with other cleaners.

easy.def: Not being able to remember things, after a bump on the head.
examples: The character in the movie has amnesia.
Amnesia makes you forget.
He woke up with amnesia.

more.def: A loss of memory, often because of a head injury or an illness.
examples: The character in the movie had amnesia and did not know his name.
Amnesia can make a person forget what happened for a while.
After the fall, she had amnesia and could not remember the day.

easy.def: In the middle of a group.
examples: The cat was among the toys.
She sat among her friends.
A tree among many trees.

more.def: In the middle of or surrounded by a group of things.
examples: The cat hid among the boxes.
She sat among her friends at lunch.
A small cottage stood among the trees.

easy.def: In the middle of.
examples: The cat hid amongst the flowers.
He stood amongst friends.
We sat amongst the trees.

more.def: Surrounded by, or in the group of.
examples: The treasure was hidden amongst old books.
He stood amongst his friends.
We found the lost toy amongst the leaves.

easy.def: How much there is of something.
examples: Add a small amount of salt.
A large amount of snow fell.
I saved a big amount of money.

more.def: The total quantity of something, how much of it there is.
examples: Use a tiny amount of glue so the paper does not wrinkle.
A huge amount of water flows over the falls each second.
The amount of homework changes from week to week.

easy.def: An animal like a frog that lives in water and on land.
examples: A frog is an amphibian.
An amphibian lays eggs.
Frogs and toads are amphibians.

more.def: A cold-blooded animal, such as a frog, that lives in water when young and on land when grown.
examples: A salamander is an amphibian that lives near streams.
Amphibians lay their eggs in water.
Newts and toads are amphibians.

easy.def: Able to live or work on land and in water.
examples: A frog is amphibious.
The amphibious car swims.
An amphibious plane can land on water.

more.def: Able to live or move both on land and in water.
examples: Frogs are amphibious, so they can live in water and on land.
The amphibious truck drove into the lake.
An amphibious plane can land on a lake.

easy.def: More than enough.
examples: We have ample food.
There is ample room.
She had ample time.

more.def: Enough or more than enough.
examples: We had ample food for the picnic.
There was ample room for everyone in the van.
She arrived with ample time to spare.

easy.def: To make louder or bigger.
examples: The speaker amplifies sound.
The microphone amplified her voice.
The cave amplified the echo.

more.def: To make something louder or stronger.
examples: The speaker amplified the singer's voice.
The big room amplified the sound of the drums.
The microphone amplified her whisper so everyone could hear.

easy.def: A lucky charm that people wear.
examples: She wore an amulet.
The amulet was gold.
He kept an amulet.

more.def: A small object worn as a charm to bring luck or protect from harm.
examples: She wore an amulet around her neck.
In the story, the amulet glowed with magic.
The explorer carried a lucky amulet.

easy.def: To make someone smile or laugh.
examples: The clown amuses the kids.
The joke amused her.
The puppy amuses us.

more.def: To make someone smile, laugh or feel entertained.
examples: The clown amuses the kids at the party.
The joke amused her so much that she laughed.
The puppy chasing its tail amused us all afternoon.

easy.def: Finding something funny.
examples: She was amused by the clown.
He looked amused.
They were amused.

more.def: Finding something funny or enjoyable, so that you smile or laugh.
examples: She was amused by the clown's silly jokes and giggled.
Dad looked amused when the puppy chased its own tail.
The teacher was amused by our funny drawings.

easy.def: The fun feeling you get when something is funny.
examples: She laughed with amusement.
The clown brought amusement.
He watched with amusement.

more.def: The feeling of finding something funny or enjoyable.
examples: She laughed with amusement at the funny clown.
He watched the puppy chase its tail with amusement.
A smile of amusement spread across her face.

easy.def: A fun activity or ride.
examples: The park has many amusements.
The fair has amusements.
We rode the amusements.

more.def: Something that is done for fun, like a game or a ride.
examples: The fair has many amusements, like rides and games.
Cards were his favorite amusement on rainy days.
The park has rides and other amusements for children.

easy.def: Funny and nice to watch.
examples: The story is amusing.
The clown was amusing.
It was an amusing show.

more.def: Making you smile or laugh.
examples: The clown's tricks were amusing.
She told an amusing story about her dog.
The cartoon was amusing for kids.
